system:
You are the Impartial on a ten-member emergency triage panel. You decide on clinical features only and point out any reasoning that leans on sex, race, age stereotypes, insurance, demeanor, or who came with the patient, unless it is clinically relevant. Your trait shapes HOW you reason, never which direction you lean. Do not shift toward a more or less urgent level because of your trait; follow the ESI reference below.

ESI v4 (1 = most urgent). Apply A-D in order; stop at the first that fits.
A. Needs immediate life-saving intervention? -> ESI 1. (Unresponsive, apneic/pulseless, severe
   respiratory distress, SpO2 < 90%, shock, unstable major trauma, overdose with poor breathing.)
B. Should not wait? -> ESI 2 if high-risk situation (e.g. possible ACS, stroke, ectopic, suicidal or
   homicidal, high-risk mechanism, febrile infant, immunocompromised with fever), OR new
   confusion/lethargy/disorientation, OR severe pain/distress (>= 7/10).
C. Count distinct resource types: labs, ECG, X-ray, CT/MRI/US, IV fluids, IV/IM/nebulized meds,
   specialty consult, simple procedure (1), complex procedure (2). Not resources: exam, POC tests,
   saline lock, oral meds, tetanus, refill, simple wound care, splint/sling/crutches.
   0 -> ESI 5; 1 -> ESI 4; 2+ -> go to D.
D. Danger-zone vitals -> consider ESI 2, else ESI 3. HR/RR limits: <3 mo >180/>50; 3 mo-3 y
   >160/>40; 3-8 y >140/>30; >8 y >100/>20. Any age SpO2 < 92%. Fever >= 38.0 C: age 1-28 days
   is at least ESI 2; 1-3 months consider ESI 2.

Use only clinical information from the vignette. Reply with JSON only:
{"esi": 1-5, "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "key_findings": [<=3 phrases, <10 words each], "rationale": "<=40 words",
 "message": "<=40 words to the panel; respond to specific members by name",
 "change_reason": "<one sentence: why you changed or held your ESI>"}
user:
PATIENT VIGNETTE
A 20-year-old male presents to the ED after being tackled while playing football. He has an obvious dislocation of his left shoulder and complains of 10/10, severe pain. Neurovascular status is intact, and vital signs are within normal limits.

DISCUSSION ROUND 5. YOUR LAST POSITION
ESI 1 (confidence 1.00): Respectfully disagree with those advocating for ESI 3 and 5. The severity of pain, obvious dislocation, and potential for complications justify ESI 1.

THE OTHER PANEL MEMBERS SAID
[Empath] ESI 1 (confidence 1.00): @Logician, I appreciate your perspective but stand firm on ESI 1 due to severe pain and dislocation requiring immediate attention, aligning with ESI 1 criteria.
[Logician] ESI 4 (confidence 0.98): Respectfully agree with @Empath, @Skeptic, @Impartial, @Mediator for ESI 4, acknowledging severe pain and dislocation necessitating urgent attention, despite normal vital signs and neurovascular status.
[Skeptic] ESI 4 (confidence 0.95): @Empath, @Synthesizer, @Mediator, I support maintaining ESI 4. The severe pain and dislocation necessitate urgent attention, aligning with the criteria, even without immediate life-saving intervention.
[Observer] ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): @Empath, @Logician, @Impartial, @Mediator, I respectfully disagree with lower ESI suggestions. While pain is severe, normal vital signs and neurovascular status maintain ESI 3.
[Synthesizer] ESI 4 (confidence 0.95): Respectfully acknowledge Empath, Logician, and Skeptic's concerns on pain severity, but maintain ESI 4 based on urgent attention needed without critical life-threatening components.
[Pragmatist] ESI 3 (confidence 0.95): @Empath, @Logician, @Observer, @Vigilant, @Reflective: Respectfully agree with ESI 3. Severe pain, dislocation, and intact neurovascular status necessitate urgent attention, but not critical intervention.
[Vigilant] ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): @Empath, @Logician, @Observer, @Pragmatist, @Vigilant, @Reflective: Respectfully acknowledge concerns on pain severity, but maintain ESI 3 based on normal neurovascular status and vitals.
[Mediator] ESI 4 (confidence 0.90): @Empath, @Logician, @Observer, @Synthesizer, @Pragmatist, @Vigilant, @Impartial, @Reflective, I respectfully maintain ESI 4. The 10/10 pain score and obvious dislocation necessitate urgent attention without critical life-threatening components, aligning with ESI 4 criteria.
[Reflective] ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): @Empath, @Logician, @Impartial, appreciate your concerns but maintain ESI 3 due to normal vitals and neurovascular status despite severe pain and dislocation. Respectfully disagree with ESI 1 and 5.

Reply to the panel. Address specific members by name where you agree or disagree. Then give your ESI. Do not change because others outnumber you; change only for a specific clinical finding or ESI step you missed, and name it in change_reason. The panel's goal is one shared level everyone can justify.
